brief.company_summary: Northwind Logistics runs route planning and real-time tracking for 400 regional delivery companies in France and Spain, handling 2 million parcel events a day. It just raised a Series B to expand into Portugal and Italy, so volume is expected to triple over 18 months.
role_requirements: 5+ years of production backend work, Python preferred
Solid PostgreSQL: schema design, indexing, query tuning
Message queues and event-driven systems experience
Owned incidents end to end and wrote postmortems
Mentoring, on-call (one week in six), clear English
brief.interview_format: 60-minute behavioral and experience interview with Julien Roux, the Engineering Manager of the Tracking team (step 2 of 4). Inference: expect past-situation questions on ownership, incidents, mentoring and teamwork.

interviewers.name: Julien Roux
interviewers.notes: Runs the 60-minute behavioral and experience interview

cv_gaps: The CV shows no mentoring or leadership of other engineers, which the role requires.
AWS experience is limited to EC2 and S3, with no ECS, RDS or SQS listed.
No evidence of owning a formal SLO like the 99.9% target.
focus_areas: Prepare a STAR story on the 3-hour migration outage: your actions, the postmortem and what changed afterwards.
Prepare a story showing influence or mentoring, such as introducing tests and CI at AgriData.
Prepare a motivation answer linking your RabbitMQ and PostgreSQL results to Northwind's scaling challenges.
probable_questions: Tell me about a production incident you led, and what you changed afterwards.
Describe a time you improved performance or reliability, and how you measured the result.
Tell me about a time you helped a less experienced colleague grow.
Describe a disagreement with a teammate or product owner and how you resolved it.
Why Northwind Logistics, and why this role now?
